note: Claim register. Only what the index CANNOT derive lives here: the statement, whether it holds, and why not when it does not. Where a claim is written, and what can make it fail, are scanned by claims_index.py -- putting them here too would be a second authority over the same facts.
namespace_warning: The id namespace is not uniform in what it points at. Some ids name a PROPOSAL (NEG-7: seventeen lenses are one grammar -- dead). Others name the REFUTATION that killed a proposal (ER-1: Orbach is saturated at 300 K -- live, and it is what killed the Er coherence claim). `names` records which, because the same status word means opposite things otherwise.

status_values.live: the statement holds and something can make it fail

claims.statement: the shipped provenance log does not reproduce under the code shipped beside it; all five replayable records mismatch

salvage.keep: The screen is the general one and it is cheap: re-run the record from its own fields and diff. It needs no domain knowledge and asks the question a provenance format exists to answer. The decisive detail is that record db001b18502f reproduces fixation_probability EXACTLY (0.65/0.35/0.0) and disagrees only on the timing fields -- so this is the same dynamics code with something changed around it, not a log of a different experiment. Mechanised as --verify, and the record now carries code_sha256 and a content-addressed run_id.
salvage.killed: the claim that these logs document the shipped code

screen.name: replay-the-log
screen.rule: Re-run a stored record from its own fields and diff the outcomes. A provenance format that has never been replayed is a format nobody has checked, and the mismatch is silent by construction.
screen.applies_when: any record, log or ledger claiming to describe a computation that could be re-run from what the record stores

claims.statement: the record's random_seed was never passed to any seeding call, so forest iterations k>0 were unreplayable

salvage.keep: A seed field that is written but never passed to a seeding call reads as reproducibility and supplies none -- and the model that WAS replayable was replayable through base_seed, the field not named seed. Worth keeping: base_seed being held fixed across iterations is correct and deliberate, because it makes successive iterations a paired comparison; it was right by accident and now says so.
salvage.killed: reproducibility of every forest record in the shipped logs

screen.name: seed-the-thing-you-record
screen.rule: Pass the recorded seed to the generator and check a re-run reproduces. A seed field that is written but never passed to a seeding call is decorative, and reads as reproducibility.
screen.applies_when: any stochastic run whose record carries a seed

claims.statement: iteration_results paired each iteration's outcomes with the next iteration's parameters

salvage.keep: The jsonl was correct and the in-memory structure was shifted by one, so the two authorities disagreed and only the one nobody plots was right. The tail coincides -- the final iteration does not call the agent -- which is how an off-by-one survives a glance at the end of the output. The check is to compare a parameter that actually MOVES; against a static one the assertion passes without testing anything.
salvage.killed: any figure or summary built from the returned structure rather than the log

screen.name: check-the-pair
screen.rule: Two quantities quoted as a pair must be mutually consistent. Check before either is used.
screen.applies_when: two quantities quoted together as a consistent pair

claims.statement: log_claim_result had no callers, so claims_tested was empty on every run

salvage.keep: A summary field that is always empty is indistinguishable from a system that tested nothing, and neither the summary nor the tests noticed. Cheap general form: for every accumulator a summary reports, grep for a caller.
salvage.killed: the claim history as an audit trail

screen.name: grep-for-a-caller
screen.rule: For every field a summary reports, find the code that writes it. An accumulator with no callers reports the same empty value as a system that ran and found nothing.
screen.applies_when: any summary, report or history object whose contents are accumulated by a separate call

claims.statement: a raising test function was recorded as a refutation; the inconclusive status was created and discarded one line later

salvage.keep: The distinction between 'measured and failed' and 'could not measure' was already in the code and was thrown away at the record boundary -- so the fix was to propagate a state that already existed, not to invent one. Reachable on the shipped defaults: the forest test formats 'N/A' with :.3f, so a collapsed forest was logged as a refuted power law. The same shape appeared in the verifier written to catch it, where a replay that raised left diffs empty and read as a clean reproduction.
salvage.killed: every 'failed' verdict in the shipped logs as evidence of refutation

screen.name: distinguish-no-evidence-from-failure
screen.rule: A score of zero for 'nothing to measure' and zero for 'measured and failed' are the same number in a ledger. Emit no record, or a distinct state.
screen.applies_when: any scoring function whose domain includes inputs it cannot score

claims.statement: the agent's num_steps branch was unreachable: one hypothesis string contained both substrings and the other was tested first

salvage.keep: The reusable form is the reachability sweep over a system's own diagnosis set -- take every diagnosis it can emit and confirm each changes something. Mechanised for this system in tests/test_adaptive_sim.py::test_every_diagnosis_tag_reaches_an_action. Also the strongest argument in the archive for not branching on generated prose: the shipped fluctuating log shows four iterations spent on one knob at a pinned outcome, and the run that worked raised num_steps by hand, out of band.
salvage.killed: the reasoning chain as a record of a search over explanations

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: fed a near-extinct forest, the agent proposes increasing competition strength

salvage.keep: ASF-5 and ASF-6 compound into a wrong action, which is the reason to care about either: the response to a dying forest is to kill it harder, recorded as a hypothesis under test. An audit that stopped at 'the exception handling is untidy' would not have reached it.
salvage.killed: the agent's proposals as directed by its observations

screen.name: follow-the-action-not-the-verdict
screen.rule: Trace what the system DOES with a verdict, not just whether the verdict is right. Two defensible-looking defects upstream can compose into an action that is the opposite of correct, and each looks like a tidiness issue alone.
screen.applies_when: any system that acts automatically on its own diagnosis

claims.statement: forest_power_law constrains the straightness of a log-log fit and not the sign of the slope; uniform[1,1000] passes 100% of draws at slope +0.919

salvage.keep: The measured pass rates are the reusable part, and the useful subtlety is that the gate is NOT vacuous -- it rejects exponential and gamma at 0% while passing uniform and lognormal at 100%. 'R2 is meaningless on log-binned data' would have been the easy verdict and it is wrong; the defect is specifically that nothing constrains the slope. Not patched: choosing a slope constraint is a claim about forests.
salvage.killed: R2 > 0.6 as evidence of a power law

screen.name: measure-the-null
screen.rule: Run the gate on data where the answer is known to be no, and count. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and a threshold with no measured false-alarm rate is not calibrated in either direction.
screen.applies_when: any threshold, gate or detector emitting a pass/fail or a score read as a rate, whose false-positive rate has not been counted on data where the answer is known to be no

claims.statement: the log-binned histogram is not divided by bin width, so the fitted slope estimates 1-alpha rather than -alpha

salvage.keep: The arithmetic is exact and reusable: with logarithmic bins the count carries a factor of the bin width, so slope = 1 - alpha. Verified at alpha 1.5/2.0/2.5/3.0 giving -0.473/-0.944/-1.442/-1.900. Consequence worth carrying: the shipped slopes of -0.369 and -0.412 are density exponents near 1.4, and a self-thinning -2 would appear here as -1, so any threshold written in the density convention is off by one.
salvage.killed: the logged slope values as density exponents

screen.name: recover-a-known-parameter
screen.rule: Feed the estimator inputs whose true parameter you set, across the range of that parameter, and check the recovered value tracks it. An estimator off by a constant offset looks perfectly well behaved on any single input.
screen.applies_when: any fitted quantity reported as a physical exponent, rate or coefficient

claims.statement: fluctuating_fixation is a claim about the step budget; sweeping num_steps alone flips the verdict at fixed biology

salvage.keep: Right-censoring reported as a biological outcome. The screen generalises past this model: vary the simulation's own resource with the physics held fixed and see whether the verdict moves. Measured, every 'coexisting' replicate is exactly a censored one -- the two fractions are equal to floating point -- which is the cheapest possible diagnostic and was one line away the whole time.
salvage.killed: coexistence probability as a statement about the strains

screen.name: sweep-the-budget-not-only-the-physics
screen.rule: Vary the simulation's own resource -- step count, sample count, cutoff -- with every substantive parameter held fixed. A verdict that flips is a verdict about the budget.
screen.applies_when: any claim read off a simulation with a finite horizon, where runs can end by exhausting it

claims.statement: switching_rate is a continuous-time generator rate consumed as a per-step Bernoulli probability, so it saturates at 1.0

salvage.keep: Rates 2.0, 5.0 and 50.0 give byte-identical outcomes. The compounding part is the reusable warning: the agent's exploration branch multiplies the rate by 1.3, so it walks into the saturated region in seven steps from the shipped default and keeps exploring a knob that has stopped responding. Not patched -- fixing it means choosing a time discretisation, which is modelling.
salvage.killed: switching_rate as a controllable parameter above 1.0

screen.name: rate-is-not-a-probability
screen.rule: A continuous-time rate used as a per-step Bernoulli probability saturates at 1 and silently stops responding. Check the dimensionless form and the value at which it pins.
screen.applies_when: any per-step stochastic update whose threshold is a quantity with units of inverse time

claims.statement: the competition radius was derived from dispersal_range, so dispersal_range 1 disables competition entirely while competition_strength stays logged nonzero

salvage.keep: One knob driving two mechanisms, and the agent can reach the value that silently switches one of them off. The fix that costs nothing is to make the derived quantity an explicit parameter defaulting to the old expression: behaviour unchanged, confound nameable. Reusable as a sweep -- take the shared knob to its extreme and check the second mechanism is still on.
salvage.killed: competition_strength as describing the competition actually applied

screen.name: one-knob-two-mechanisms
screen.rule: Derive one mechanism's parameter from another's and the two can never be varied independently. Sweep the shared knob to its extreme and check whether the second mechanism is still on.
screen.applies_when: any parameter whose value is computed from another parameter belonging to a different mechanism

claims.statement: exploration_rate was stored and never read; 0.0 and 1.0 gave identical behaviour

salvage.keep: The third instance of the unread-parameter shape after GR-2's bands_per_octave and GLY-3's sub_glyphs, and the detector is the same two-line sweep: run at both extremes and diff. Cheap enough to run over every declared parameter in a module, which is the mechanisation nothing has yet.
salvage.killed: exploration_rate as a tunable

screen.name: set-it-to-both-extremes
screen.rule: Run the code at a parameter's extreme values and diff the output. Identical output means the parameter is not read.
screen.applies_when: any declared parameter, option or weight whose effect on the output has not been demonstrated

claims.statement: forest_species_coexistence returns the same verdict for competitive exclusion and for an empty grid

salvage.keep: Measured over 5 seeds at every setting the agent can reach, richness is 3,3,3,3,3; the only configuration that fails the claim is high mortality, where richness is 0 because the forest is dead. So the claim's one reachable failure mode is not the one it is named for. The remedy reuses ASF-5's inconclusive channel rather than inventing a coexistence threshold, which would have been a claim about forests.
salvage.killed: richness > 1 as a test of coexistence

screen.name: distinguish-no-evidence-from-failure
screen.rule: A score of zero for 'nothing to measure' and zero for 'measured and failed' are the same number in a ledger. Emit no record, or a distinct state.
screen.applies_when: any scoring function whose domain includes inputs it cannot score

claims.statement: the auto-generated claim's description asserted a correlation with seed_rate that its single-run threshold test never varied

salvage.keep: Two defects in one line and only the second is interesting: the description names a correlation nothing sweeps, and the threshold is written in the density-exponent convention while the tested quantity is a binned-count slope (ASF-9), so it fails on arrival at the observed slopes. Correcting the description was right; testing the correlation needs a sweep the loop cannot express, which is open problem ASF-A.
salvage.killed: the generated claim as evidence about seed_rate

screen.name: does-the-test-test-the-description
screen.rule: Read the claim's stated content and its assertion side by side. A claim about a relationship cannot be tested at one point, and a threshold inherits the units of whatever produced the number.
screen.applies_when: any claim carrying both a prose description and an executable test

claims.statement: claim ids embedded int(time.time()), so two claims generated in the same second collide

salvage.keep: Minor and measured rather than argued: generating two claims in a loop produces one id. Kept because a collision in an id namespace makes the claim history unreadable in exactly the place ASF-4 already made it empty.
salvage.killed: generated claim ids as unique

screen.name: generate-two-and-compare
screen.rule: Call the id generator twice in immediate succession and compare. Any id derived from wall-clock seconds collides under a loop.
screen.applies_when: any identifier derived from a coarse clock

claims.statement: a registry is bookkeeping, not a pin; a template pin coupling to something non-topological removes the core zero mode

salvage.keep: The correct half is load-bearing and was kept: topological charge is invariant while core POSITION is a zero mode. The remedy was wrong, not the finding. A pin coupling to something non-topological removes the zero mode -- measured, 100% hop at k_p = 0 and 0% at k_p >= 0.01, charge conserved throughout.
salvage.killed: a registry as a vortex pin -- bookkeeping costs nothing to violate

claims.statement: piezoresistive readout gives dR/R about 9% at 0.1% strain, gauge factor about 121 along <110>
the reported geometric_speedup was a point-count ratio times a symmetry factor, with no clock in it; timed, the adaptive path is 2x-50x slower than the uniform baseline

salvage.keep: The measurement is the reusable part and it took one afternoon: uniform grid vs adaptive octree, same sources, same optimizer, best-of-N wall clock. `generateUniformGrid` already existed and had never been called by the solver, so the baseline was there all along. What survives the correction is the geometry: at resolution 32 the octree evaluates 15x fewer points and the field evaluation over those points really is ~26x faster (ENG-5). The claim that was wrong is that this had been measured.
salvage.killed: the 15x-33x speedup figure, and every roadmap phase target written as a multiple of it

screen.name: time-it-against-a-baseline
screen.rule: A number called a speedup must come from two clocks on two runs of the same problem. A ratio of counts, of points or of operations, is a ratio of counts; report it under that name.
screen.applies_when: any performance claim quoted as a multiplier

claims.statement: naive_points was hardcoded to 32**3 while resolution was a documented parameter that reached nothing

salvage.keep: Fourth instance of the unread-parameter shape after GR-2's bands_per_octave, GLY-3's sub_glyphs and ASF-13's exploration_rate, and the detector is the same two-line sweep: run at both extremes and diff. The docstring named a 'uniform fallback' path that does not exist in the module, which is the tell -- a parameter documented for a code path nobody wrote.
salvage.killed: resolution as a parameter that affected anything

screen.name: set-it-to-both-extremes
screen.rule: Run the code at a parameter's extreme values and diff the output. Identical output means the parameter is not read.
screen.applies_when: any declared parameter, option or weight whose effect on the output has not been demonstrated

claims.statement: the reported figure multiplied in a symmetry reduction the solver explicitly does not take

salvage.keep: The call site's own comment says it: 'we compute all but report the potential reduction'. Measured, a symmetric configuration reports 1.50x more speedup while taking 1.89x more wall clock, so the metric moves opposite to the truth exactly where the geometry is best. The general form is worth keeping: a saving may enter an efficiency figure only if the code took it.
salvage.killed: the symmetry factor as a contribution to measured performance

screen.name: credit-only-work-actually-skipped
screen.rule: A saving may enter a performance figure only if the code took it. If a comment says the saving is available but not exploited, the figure is counting work that was done.
screen.applies_when: any efficiency figure built from a reduction factor rather than from elapsed time

claims.statement: averageSpeedup reported the last run while history accumulated every run and was read by nothing

salvage.keep: Small, measured rather than argued: two runs at 15.24 and 22.88 reported 22.9 against a true mean of 19.06. Kept because the name is the whole defect -- a field called an average that is not one is read as one, and the data to compute it properly was already being stored.
salvage.killed: averageSpeedup as an average

screen.name: does-the-test-test-the-description
screen.rule: Read the claim's stated content and its assertion side by side. A claim about a relationship cannot be tested at one point, and a threshold inherits the units of whatever produced the number.
screen.applies_when: any claim carrying both a prose description and an executable test

claims.statement: SpatialGrid.createRegion emits one sample point per leaf region, so the solver makes one numpy call per point and defeats its own vectorisation

salvage.keep: This is the actionable half of ENG-1 and the reason the roadmap's near-term item is a measurement rather than a multiplier. Batching the same points into one call: 0.0023 s against 0.0597 s, a 26x overhead removed and a 27x gain on the field evaluation. But the octree decomposition costs 0.0645 s against the uniform path's 0.0713 s total, so batching alone lands at 1.07x end to end -- both halves have to come down, and knowing that before starting is worth more than the 26x. Left in place deliberately; the fix changes solver output ordering and the per-region efficiency averaging.
salvage.killed: the adaptive decomposition as delivering a speedup in its current form

screen.name: time-it-against-a-baseline
screen.rule: A number called a speedup must come from two clocks on two runs of the same problem. A ratio of counts, of points or of operations, is a ratio of counts; report it under that name.
screen.applies_when: any performance claim quoted as a multiplier

claims.statement: simdEfficiency is a function of chunk length alone and reports 12.5% for every configuration ever run

salvage.keep: A metric that returns the same number for one charge and for four is a constant wearing the name of a measurement, and the cause is ENG-5: one point per region means one lane of eight, always. It becomes informative for free once ENG-5 is addressed, which is why it is reported with the constancy stated rather than removed.
salvage.killed: simdEfficiency as evidence of vectorisation quality

screen.name: vary-the-input-and-watch-the-metric
screen.rule: Feed the metric two configurations that should score differently. A value that does not move is a constant wearing the name of a measurement.
screen.applies_when: any reported efficiency, score or quality number whose response to its input has not been shown

claims.statement: 109.47 degrees is the tetrahedral maximin bound, from |sum v_i|^2 = 4 + 2 sum v_i.v_j >= 0

salvage.keep: The two-line identity |sum v_i|^2 = 4 + 2 sum v_i.v_j >= 0 proves the 109.47 degree maximin bound outright. It replaced a numerical search that stalled half a degree short -- worth remembering when an optimiser is standing in for an identity.

claims.statement: cubic symmetry forces a rank-2 transport tensor to lambda*I, so conductivity is isotropic

salvage.keep: Neumann's principle on a cubic crystal forces any rank-2 transport tensor to lambda*I. Free to check, kills every 'preferred direction in cubic Si' claim at once, and generalises to every material in that point group.
salvage.killed: directional thermal or electrical transport anisotropy in cubic silicon

screen.name: neumann-cubic
screen.rule: Neumann's principle: a rank-2 tensor invariant under a cubic group is lambda*I. Any 'preferred direction in a cubic crystal' claim dies by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a claim of directional anisotropy in a material whose point group forbids it

claims.statement: Orbach is saturated at 300 K, not merely open

salvage.keep: The Orbach screen generalises to any deep-level or rare-earth coherence claim in any host: compare the crystal-field gap to kT, check the Bose occupation, and if Delta << kT the rate is linear in T and the claim is finished. Two lines, no apparatus. Er's 1.5 um optical transition is untouched and is where the real literature works -- at cryogenic temperature.
salvage.killed: Er3+ holds T2 = 166 ms at 300 K in silicon

screen.name: orbach-vs-kT
screen.rule: Compare the crystal-field gap to kT. If Delta << kT the Orbach rate goes linear in T and any coherence claim at that temperature is finished.
screen.applies_when: a claim of retained coherence in a solid at a stated temperature, where a crystal-field or level splitting exists

claims.statement: no Er gap mode exists in the searched window

salvage.keep: The gap-mode mass criterion m_impurity < m_host is a one-line screen for every local-vibrational-mode proposal. It killed the $10k Er search and the 'P local mode at ~500 cm^-1' claim in the same stroke, for free.
salvage.killed: a $10k search for an Er local vibrational mode at 300-400 cm^-1

screen.name: gap-mode-mass
screen.rule: A local vibrational mode above the host band needs m_impurity < m_host. Heavier impurity, no gap mode, no search worth funding.
screen.applies_when: a claim that an impurity produces a vibrational mode above the host band

claims.statement: the same criterion kills 'P local mode at ~500 cm^-1'

salvage.keep: Same mass criterion, second target. That a single screen kills two independent claims in one archive is the argument for writing screens down rather than re-deriving them.
salvage.killed: a phosphorus local mode at ~500 cm^-1

screen.name: gap-mode-mass
screen.rule: A local vibrational mode above the host band needs m_impurity < m_host. Heavier impurity, no gap mode, no search worth funding.
screen.applies_when: a claim that an impurity produces a vibrational mode above the host band

claims.statement: the stated (omega, k) pair is inconsistent by ~8x

salvage.keep: Checking (omega, k) for mutual consistency before quoting either is a two-line screen and it caught an 8x discrepancy.
salvage.killed: the stated omega and k_well pair

screen.name: check-the-pair
screen.rule: Two quantities quoted as a pair must be mutually consistent. Check before either is used.
screen.applies_when: two quantities quoted together as a consistent pair

claims.statement: the stated implant dose is achievable
a 5 um Si cell carries 4e-19 A m2, eleven orders below a Hall sensor and seven below a SQUID

salvage.keep: The instrument-floor comparison is now repo_guard.reach and it is free to run. Everything above the physics layer in Magnetic-bridge.md -- the FSM, the protocol structure, the hardware list -- was sound and was kept; only the transduction was replaced, by strain at 40x the authority.
salvage.killed: a magnetic state channel in silicon, 11 orders below a Hall sensor

screen.name: instrument-floor
screen.rule: Compute the signal in the instrument's own units and divide by its noise floor before designing anything around reading it.
screen.applies_when: any claim that a stated physical quantity will be READ by a named instrument

claims.statement: the eight implant states are separable at >3 sigma in (R_s, carrier type, n)
NOVEL is reachable with a stable anchor logged

salvage.keep: The general form: a route that appends a zero-weight candidate silently disables any branch guarded on the candidate list being empty. A branch contributes only with positive evidence now, and NOVEL records the negative evidence it rests on.
salvage.killed: the four-way router, which forked one way whenever an anchor was logged

claims.statement: and it emits the experiment that route implies
anchor_dev is a deviation against an explicit tolerance
and the tolerance actually gates it
NOISE_AS_SIGNAL has a sample floor and a scaled band
a lag scan sees the rider periods a fixed lag cannot

salvage.keep: rho(lag) = cos(2*pi*lag/T) is the whole lesson: a detector that probes a continuous space at one fixed coordinate is blind wherever the response vanishes there. Reusable for any single-point probe, not just autocorrelation.
salvage.killed: the fixed-lag-3 structure detector, 0% power at periods 4, 10, 12, 14, 16

screen.name: probe-the-whole-family
screen.rule: Write the response as a function of the probe coordinate and find its zeros. A detector fixed at one coordinate has zero power wherever the response vanishes there.
screen.applies_when: a detector that samples a continuous parameter at one fixed value

claims.statement: MISSING_VARIABLE is a corrected binomial tail, not 1.5x base

salvage.keep: The measured null rates are the reusable part: 34.7%, 34.0%, 41.0%, rising with n because more bins clear the sample floor. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and the number was a third.
salvage.killed: rate > 1.5x base as a covariate concentration test

screen.name: measure-the-null
screen.rule: Run the gate on data where the answer is known to be no, and count. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and a threshold with no measured false-alarm rate is not calibrated in either direction.
screen.applies_when: any threshold, gate or detector emitting a pass/fail or a score read as a rate, whose false-positive rate has not been counted on data where the answer is known to be no

claims.statement: and it still finds a real concentration
residual membership is by index, not dict equality
deepen requires a tighter band or a named axis
self-initiated actuation is metered, capped and credited
a shape cannot be scalarized without naming the projection
claim ids come from live ids, not the log line count
the correlated series is uncensored

salvage.keep: Censoring biases rather than blinds -- the censored series still returned STRUCTURED, at lag 4 against a true half-period of 5. A confident wrong answer is worse than silence, and that is the general shape.
salvage.killed: feeding the correlation branch only band-breaking readings

screen.name: compare-filtered-to-full
screen.rule: Run the analysis on the full record and on the filtered one and compare the ANSWERS, not the detection rates. Filtering biases before it blinds.
screen.applies_when: an analysis run on a filtered subset of a record

claims.statement: lag is a duration when there is a clock
and it is calibrated on an irregular clock
and no period is claimed
multiplicity correction is BH, and the gain is stated small

salvage.keep: The honest negative: at k=1 Benjamini-Hochberg IS Bonferroni, so with one true effect the swap buys exactly nothing. The larger lever was found by measuring instead -- the exact binomial is discrete, so the achieved level sits near 1% against a nominal 5%.
salvage.killed: the expectation that the FDR swap would recover meaningful power

claims.statement: verify_edge_measurement computes delta_pct = 100*(measured/pred - 1) and raises ZeroDivisionError whenever the claim's predicted value is zero

salvage.keep: Zero is reachable two ways that both occur in the shipped demo's own domain: a rotate edge declares an angle and 0 is legal, and an acyclic network's integrity claim is exactly 0.0. A relative error is undefined at zero for every claim type, not just this one -- the ledger's other domains compare against nonzero physical rates, which is why the pattern survived there.
salvage.killed: verify_edge_measurement on rotate edges and on integrity claims

claims.statement: an acyclic design records an integrity claim of value 0.0, so a correct chain scores worst and writes the value GB-1 crashes on

salvage.keep: Not a bug in audit(): a network with no cycles genuinely has nothing to be consistent about, and 0.0 is the honest answer to a question that should not have been asked. The bridge should decline to write an integrity claim for an acyclic network rather than write a zero, because the ledger cannot tell 'no evidence' from 'failed'. The demo's own DEMO 5 does exactly this.
salvage.killed: the integrity claim as meaningful for a network without cycles

screen.name: distinguish-no-evidence-from-failure
screen.rule: A score of zero for 'nothing to measure' and zero for 'measured and failed' are the same number in a ledger. Emit no record, or a distinct state.
screen.applies_when: any scoring function whose domain includes inputs it cannot score

claims.statement: the integrity claim's failure text describes a threshold test while the record encodes a two-sided band around the value

salvage.keep: A claim record carries both what a verifier will compute and what a human will read, and here they are different tests. The text also cites 3.618, which GI-12 shows that score cannot reach. Cheap general check: read the failure string against the tol_frac in the same record.
salvage.killed: the failure text as a description of the encoded test

claims.statement: three unsourced tolerances (0.05 edge, phi^-9 cycle, 0.10 integrity) and a drift band of (1+t)^2 rather than a doubled tolerance

salvage.keep: The drift band is a real design choice and a defensible one -- it is multiplicative, which suits a ratio claim -- but it reads as 2x tolerance and diverges from it as t grows: at t = 0.5 it is [0.25, 2.25] rather than [0, 2]. Naming it in the docstring costs one line. The three tolerances need sources rather than defaults before any verdict from them means anything.
salvage.killed: the three defaults as calibrated tolerances

claims.statement: LEDGER is a relative path and append_geo_claims does an unlocked read-modify-write, matching the 23 sites in fabrication/

salvage.keep: The relative path is the sharper half and it is not in the original analysis of fabrication/: the ledger written depends on the working directory, so running from the repo root and from fabrication/ produces two ledgers that do not know about each other. Fixing it in one of 24 places makes the split worse, so it stays until all 24 move together. Open problem GI-10.
salvage.killed: the ledger as a single authority regardless of where a tool is run

claims.statement: IntegrityMonitor predictions are seeded from the design value, not the measurement, so a measured error propagates nowhere

salvage.keep: The module answers 'is this part where the drawing says', which is a real question and the one it can be trusted for. What it does NOT answer, and reads as if it does, is 'given this part came out wrong, is the next one still compatible'. Naming which of the two a tool answers is most of the value of auditing it, and full_report now carries predictions_use_measurements so a caller cannot assume the second.
salvage.killed: the field guide's stated purpose of catching a mis-cut part before the next one is committed

screen.name: test-the-distinguishing-operation
screen.rule: Apply the operation that is supposed to separate the states and check every invariant the representation exposes. If none move, the representation is blind to it.
screen.applies_when: any encoding claiming N distinct states, where some operation is supposed to separate them

claims.statement: the INTEGRITY_THRESHOLD clause in full_report is unsatisfiable: integrity is a product of two fractions so is at most 1.0, and the clause tests it against 1.809

salvage.keep: phi^2 + 1 = 3.618 is a correct constant that does no work anywhere in the module, so removing it costs nothing and keeping it costs a reader's trust. The general form: a threshold and the quantity it gates must be shown to share a range before the comparison means anything -- one line, and it is the same check that killed BLOCKAGE in bridges/.
salvage.killed: phi^2 + 1 as a coherence bound on anything this module computes

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: check() keeps the minimum-error prediction over all sources, so a design with two routes of different product is resolved in the measurement's favour and reported trusted

salvage.keep: The redundancy is free evidence and is being spent to hide a contradiction rather than to find one: two routes disagreeing IS the finding, and reporting the spread instead of the minimum turns the same computation into a design audit. On a path-consistent design the O(N^2) walk returns one value from every source, so nothing is lost by changing it.
salvage.killed: a trusted verdict as evidence the design is self-consistent

screen.name: report-the-spread-not-the-best-fit
screen.rule: When a check has several independent routes to the same quantity, report their spread. Keeping the closest one to the measurement converts disagreement into agreement and destroys the evidence.
screen.applies_when: any verification with more than one path from premises to a predicted value

claims.statement: reconstruct() implements neither the averaging nor the path weighting its docstring promises; the first edge to reach a node wins, so insertion order decides

salvage.keep: The docstring is a usable specification of what the function should do -- confidence-weighted average over trusted paths -- and it is worth keeping as the target rather than deleting to match the code. The measurable form of the defect is cheap: build the same graph twice with the edges added in each order and compare, which is a general test for any first-writer-wins propagation.
salvage.killed: a reconstructed value as better than a single-path estimate

claims.statement: IntegrityReport.reconstructed is declared on the dataclass and never assigned, so it is None on every report the module produces

salvage.keep: A declared-and-never-written field is found by one loop over the constructor's outputs, and it is worth looking for because it usually means a second code path was planned and the first one shipped. Here full_report fills the same value from a separate dict, so the two are one field apart from being a duplicate authority.

claims.statement: reconstruct() returns {} from a single measurement, and a forward-only chain reports its first node untrusted on perfect measurements

salvage.keep: The rule is simple and belongs in the field guide rather than the code: a node nothing points at cannot be predicted, so build every network with edges in both directions, and reconstruction needs two surviving measurements that agree, not one. The drop's own timber-frame example had forward edges only and flagged a correctly cut brace; the README's nautilus example added both directions and did not.
salvage.killed: the documented one-measurement emergency reconstruction

claims.statement: the field guide's speed-of-sound correction was 6%; the true shift from +20 C to -40 C is 10.6%

salvage.keep: c(T) = 331.3 + 0.606*T is within 0.32% of the exact sqrt(1+T/273.15) form at -40 C and 0.52% at -50 C, so the linear approximation is fine over the stated range and only the arithmetic downstream of it was wrong. 343.0 m/s hardcoded across fabrication/ is the +15 C value. pipe_modes, box_modes, cylinder_modes and ka_check already accept c=, so this is a threading job from a recorded temperature, not a physics change.
salvage.killed: the 6% figure a reader would have compensated by

claims.statement: core.audit()'s integrity_score responds to the geometry: randomising every edge factor drops it from 2.000 to a mean of 0.014 over 200 draws

salvage.keep: The one positive result in this folder, and worth recording as one. The null harness is cheap here because a geometric network has an obvious structure-destroying perturbation -- randomise the edge factors, keep the graph and the weights. Running it first also bounds what the other findings can mean: audit() is measuring something real and measuring it wrongly, which is a different repair from measuring nothing.

claims.statement: cycle closure is evaluated at the single point x = 1, so any affine cycle map with a + b = 1 is reported consistent without being the identity

salvage.keep: The general rule is one line and it transfers: an affine map is two numbers, so testing it at one point cannot determine it. Either evaluate at two points or compare (a, b) to (1, 0) directly -- the code already computes both in _compose_transforms and then throws b away into a single scalar. Pure-scale cycles have b = 0 and are unaffected, which is exactly why every demo and every shipped test misses it: they build only scale edges, and `compose` is the kind that breaks it.
salvage.killed: closure error as evidence that a cycle composes to the identity

screen.name: probe-at-two-points
screen.rule: A test that evaluates a transform at one input cannot tell it from any other transform with the same fixed point. Evaluate at two, or compare the transform's parameters to identity directly.
screen.applies_when: any check that validates a map by running it on a single test value

claims.statement: integrity_score = base_score * (1 + mean_edge_weight), where weight is author-declared and only ever adds: zero confidence still scores the full consistency fraction

salvage.keep: Two quantities are being multiplied that answer different questions -- how much of the network closes, and how sure the author was -- and the product has the units of neither. Measured: weights alone move the score across 1.2298-1.7248 with the geometry untouched, and declaring weight 0.0 costs nothing because the term is (1 + w) rather than w. Reporting the two separately costs nothing and makes both readable. The same arithmetic explains why INTEGRITY_THRESHOLD is unreachable: the ceiling at w <= 1 is 2.0.
salvage.killed: integrity_score as a single comparable number

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: correct() reaches cycle consistency by splitting the error across the cycle rather than restoring the wrong edge

salvage.keep: The distinction worth keeping: making a model self-consistent and making it correct are different operations, and only the first is decidable from the model alone. Measured on the drop's own injected defect -- an edge 23.6% high converges to +11.9% with its inverse partner at -9.5%, and audit() then reports 5/5 consistent. Any correction that only sees the residual has this property; restoring the right value needs an external reference, which is what the measurements are for.
salvage.killed: a post-correct() audit as evidence the design is right

screen.name: consistency-is-not-correctness
screen.rule: A procedure that minimises internal disagreement can always reach zero by moving everything. Check what it moved, not just that it converged.
screen.applies_when: any iterative correction driven by a self-consistency residual

claims.statement: _inverse_apply returns float('inf') on a zero factor while its only caller guards with except (ZeroDivisionError, OverflowError)

salvage.keep: A sentinel return and an exception guard written by two authors for the same failure, neither aware of the other, so the guard never fires and inf enters a reconstruction as a value. Found for free by the interim core.py reconstruction, which RAISED here -- guessing the safer behaviour is how you miss a bug, and that is the reusable lesson about reconstructing a missing module.
salvage.killed: the except clause in reconstruct() as protection

claims.statement: hash() is documented as a hash of network topology and relations and is also a hash of insertion order

salvage.keep: to_dict() lists nodes and edges in insertion order, so the same network built two ways hashes differently -- which matters because the hash is what a ledger entry would use to say 'this is the artifact I predicted'. Sorting by node id in to_dict() fixes it. The shipped test hashes one object twice, so it asserts the property that cannot fail and not the one that is false.
salvage.killed: hash() as an identity for a network across two constructions

claims.statement: three of the drop's 20 tests cannot fail: the audit bounds hold by construction, the hash test reuses one object, and the correct() fixture is already consistent

salvage.keep: The fixture is the sharp one: 2.5 x 0.4 = 1.0 exactly, so a pair commented 'slightly wrong' is exactly right, and correct() -- the function with two of this folder's findings in it -- is never run on an inconsistent network by anything in the suite. Checking a fixture's arithmetic before trusting what a test covers is two lines and it is where the coverage actually went. The suite is kept and vendored as evidence rather than deleted.
salvage.killed: the 20-test suite as validation of audit(), hash() or correct()

screen.name: check-the-fixture-arithmetic
screen.rule: Before believing a test covers a case, evaluate its fixture. A fixture meant to be wrong and accidentally right silently removes the test.
screen.applies_when: any test whose fixture is a hand-written constant meant to violate a condition

claims.statement: T = outer(v,v) cannot see the sign of v, so states i and 7-i are identical in every invariant
index parity equals site type, 8/8

salvage.keep: Index parity IS site type, verified against the diamond-cubic basis, which hands the 3-bit address space a free single-bit error-detecting code -- exactly what the 'geometric error correction' claim wanted and could not derive. The carrier is J3, not the trace: trace and J2 are identical across all eight states.
salvage.killed: the trace as the state-distinguishing invariant

claims.statement: every NOT crosses sublattices, so every NOT is a Frenkel pair

salvage.keep: NOT crosses the sublattice, so every NOT is a Frenkel pair at ~4.75 eV. That converts a gate-set question into an energy budget, which is answerable. The honest state space is 4 states plus a site-type flag.
salvage.killed: NOT as a free unary operation on the 8-state encoding

screen.name: frenkel-cost
screen.rule: An operation that moves an atom between sublattices costs a Frenkel pair. Price it before calling the operation free.
screen.applies_when: a claimed operation that moves an atom between sublattices or sites

claims.statement: bridges/glyph_state_encoder.py did not compile: two complete encoders pasted end to end, a second `from __future__` at line 720

salvage.keep: The two halves are the only two independent statements in the repository of what the twelve glyphs mean. The superseded half's phase_space declarations survive as PHASE_SPACE_SPEC in the replacement, which is what lets the surviving classifier be scored against a specification it did not author instead of against its own thresholds.
salvage.killed: every import of bridges.glyph_state_encoder, and with it any use of the glyph layer at all

screen.name: compile-every-file
screen.rule: A merge or paste that concatenates rather than resolves leaves a file that reads correctly in fragments and compiles in none. Compile every .py in the folder before trusting any result from it -- ast.parse is not enough, since a misplaced future import parses and does not compile.
screen.applies_when: a folder whose files arrived by paste or merge rather than by incremental edit

claims.statement: BLOCKAGE is unsatisfiable: its rule needs pressure > 0.5 and total_magnitude < 0.5, and pressure is a non-negative term of that total

salvage.keep: Reachability of a classifier's outputs is decidable by inspection whenever a rule constrains both a term and the sum it belongs to. One glyph in twelve was dead and no sampling was needed to show it -- 20 000 random draws only confirmed what two lines of arithmetic already gave.
salvage.killed: the BLOCKAGE state

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: the rule ladder is order-dependent with the order undeclared; recovery of the intended glyph from its own specification is 7 of 12

salvage.keep: Scoring a classifier against exemplars built from a SEPARATE statement of intent tells a precedence bug from a logic bug. The HEAT_FLUX exemplar satisfies RE_NORMALIZE's own rule, so no rule here is wrong -- the order in which they are tried is what decides, and it is written nowhere.
salvage.killed: the reading of 7/12 as a logic error

screen.name: score-against-a-spec-you-did-not-write
screen.rule: Build the test inputs from a statement of intent written apart from the implementation under test. Exemplars derived from the implementation's own thresholds measure nothing.
screen.applies_when: a classifier whose thresholds and whose test inputs would otherwise share an author

claims.statement: sub_glyphs is a function of the primary glyph alone and carries no information about the reading

salvage.keep: The screen that found it is the GIES-2 / KEA-7 one carried into a third formalism: vary the thing the field is supposed to track and check the field moves. Two reading sets differing in every magnitude produce byte-identical sub_glyphs, and the constant travels into both entropy() and the wire format under the name 'secondary states'.
salvage.killed: sub_glyphs as evidence of anything about the measurement

claims.statement: the phase-space classifier reaches 5 of 12 glyphs and returns FELT_COHERENT for an empty reading set

salvage.keep: Its phase_space declarations are the only description of what each glyph MEANS written apart from a classifier, and they became PHASE_SPACE_SPEC. The cause generalises: every scoring branch sat behind `if condition in readings` where the conditions are tokens like low_fear that are never reading keys, so the guard silently deleted the ladder beneath it. A dead channel then read as the healthy state.
salvage.killed: the phase-space glyph encoder, now legacy/glyph_state_encoder_phase_space.py, and its untested decay/energy layer with it

claims.statement: the codec is lossy and documented as if it were not, and an uncertainty above 1.0 is reachable from a legal reading and raises struct.error

salvage.keep: Two separate things worth keeping: the repo's lossless-round-trip convention needs an explicit exception rather than a silent one, and a field packed into one byte needs its domain checked against the domain of what feeds it. uncertainty is (max-min)/2 over magnitudes documented on [0, inf), so the byte overflows at a magnitude spread above 2.

claims.statement: the demo constructed an empty SensorSuite, classified six VOIDs, and printed 'operational'

salvage.keep: A demo that cannot fail is not evidence the module works. The fix costs one assertion -- count distinct outputs over the demo's own inputs and exit nonzero below a floor -- and it converts the demo from a advertisement into a test. The try/except that preferred the real empty suite over the populated mock is the general trap: the fallback had the data and the preferred path had none.
salvage.killed: the 'operational' banner as evidence

screen.name: demo-must-be-able-to-fail
screen.rule: A __main__ block that prints success unconditionally is an advertisement. Give it one assertion about its own output and a nonzero exit.
screen.applies_when: a module whose only exercise is a __main__ demo

claims.statement: encode() needed `time`, imported only inside __main__, so the module raised NameError for every importer while the demo passed

salvage.keep: The __main__ block is a scope boundary in one direction only: names bound there become module globals when the file is RUN and do not exist when it is IMPORTED. So a demo can supply a binding the library needs, and then the demo is exercising a different module than the one anyone imports. Import the module in a test rather than running it.
salvage.killed: the demo's pass as evidence the library worked

screen.name: import-it-do-not-run-it
screen.rule: Exercise a module through an import in a test, not through its __main__ block. Running the file can bind names that importing it does not.
screen.applies_when: a module with a __main__ demo and no test that imports it

claims.statement: the phi band edges are not monotonic: the loop overshoots f_max and then appends it, so the last interval is reversed and empty

salvage.keep: Two defects for the price of one inspection: a band that no input can enter, and a band above it running past the f_max the caller asked for, so components between f_max and the overshoot are counted and everything above the overshoot is dropped silently. Any geometric-progression edge builder has this shape -- the exit test fires after the step, not before.
salvage.killed: f_max as the stated upper limit of the analysis

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: bands_per_octave is stored and never read; every value gives byte-identical band edges

salvage.keep: An argument that looks like the resolution control and is not. Found by the cheapest possible test -- construct with two extreme values and compare the derived state -- which is worth running against every constructor parameter that is supposed to change something.
salvage.killed: bands_per_octave as a tuning knob

screen.name: test-the-distinguishing-operation
screen.rule: Apply the operation that is supposed to separate the states and check every invariant the representation exposes. If none move, the representation is blind to it.
screen.applies_when: any encoding claiming N distinct states, where some operation is supposed to separate them

claims.statement: the power-law fit is built from every populated band including the peaks it is then used to judge, contradicting its own comment

salvage.keep: The bias has a direction worth stating: including anomalies in the baseline raises it, so the method misses anomalies, and it misses more of them the more of the spectrum is anomalous -- weakest exactly when there is most to find. A robust fit or a leave-one-out baseline fixes it; the shape is P-SELF-SUPPLIED-FALSIFIER in a spectral estimator.

claims.statement: detect_injection flags 15.7% of bins when both series are independent draws of the same noise process

salvage.keep: For iid exponential numerator and denominator the analytic false-alarm rate is 1/(1+t), which at t = 2.3156 is 30.2% -- so the measured 15.7% on Rayleigh amplitudes is the expected order and the gate is behaving exactly as its arithmetic says. The fix is the FCL-5/6 pair the field loop already needed: a permutation null and a correction over the number of bins tested. injection_score cannot be read as a rate until both exist.
salvage.killed: injection_score as a rate of anything

screen.name: measure-the-null
screen.rule: Run the gate on data where the answer is known to be no, and count. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and a threshold with no measured false-alarm rate is not calibrated in either direction.
screen.applies_when: any threshold, gate or detector emitting a pass/fail or a score read as a rate, whose false-positive rate has not been counted on data where the answer is known to be no

claims.statement: detect_injection returns a dict with no injections key when called without a baseline, so the documented fallback raises KeyError in the caller

salvage.keep: The fallback itself is intended and documented; only the silent shape change is not. It fails for exactly the callers who captured no baseline -- the cold-workshop case the field guide is written for -- which is the general lesson: a fallback path is used by the least-equipped caller, so it needs the tightest contract, not the loosest.

claims.statement: exactly one minimum, at the ideal centre

salvage.keep: The Keating parameters alpha = 48.1 and beta = 12.0 N/m are correct and reusable. 'Eight octahedral faces' is the one correct use of that terminology in the whole set. And the general form of the error is a screen: a sum of squares has ONE zero, so any 'N degenerate minima' claim about a VFF model is checkable by inspection before anyone runs an optimiser.
salvage.killed: the 8-state clamped Keating encoding, its gate set and its ALU

screen.name: sum-of-squares-has-one-zero
screen.rule: A sum of squares has exactly one zero. Any 'N degenerate minima' claim about a positive-definite form is checkable before an optimiser is written.
screen.applies_when: a claim of N degenerate minima in a positive-definite energy form

claims.statement: no lattice separation lands on phi*a

salvage.keep: The phi-spacing check is reusable: enumerate the real lattice separations before claiming any of them lands on an irrational multiple of a.
salvage.killed: phi-spaced sites coinciding with lattice separations

claims.statement: energy is exactly even, so vertex and face are degenerate

salvage.keep: The tetrahedral identities sum(v_k) = 0 and v_k.v_l = -d0^2/3 are exact and reusable anywhere the cluster appears. The error's general form is the more valuable half: an encoding must be tested against the operation that is supposed to distinguish its states, which is the same blindness GIES-1 hit in a formalism that never met this one.
salvage.killed: vertex-versus-face distinguishability in the clamped cluster

screen.applies_when: any encoding claiming N distinct states, where some operation is supposed to separate them

claims.statement: An archive is a dissipative structure. Lifetime is set by `sigma - W_care/T`, not by the medium.
Finite-time erasure costs `kT ln2 + C/tau`; resurfacing of an overwritten trace scales as `tau^-1`
Dependency re-rooting is the correct update operation; radiate and recenter are the only two evidence moves
Seventeen cultural and scientific lenses are surface renderings of one deep grammar
claims.because: randomly-coefficiented lenses of the same functional form reproduce the reported correlation floor; see Negentropic/lens_collapse_test.py

salvage.keep: The seventeen lenses remain a usable phrasebook between vocabularies -- what died is the claim that they are ONE grammar, not that translating between them helps. And the harness that killed it generalised: repo_guard.null_harness now runs the same test on anything.

screen.name: null-harness
screen.rule: Replace the structure you claim is doing the work with noise of the same shape. If the result survives, it was the shape.
screen.applies_when: any claim whose evidence is statistical, or whose structure could be replaced by noise of the same shape

claims.statement: A structure persists iff it exports entropy at least as fast as it produces it: `Phi = -S_exchange_dot - sigma >= 0`
A cycle after inversion is a contradiction detector: two claims cannot both be foundational to each other, so one is wrong
Recenter cost = edges reversed ∝ path length, so archives that recenter often evolve toward shallow, wide topology
The validation gate is load-bearing: an archive rooted on an unvalidated node degrades faster than one rooted on a confirmed one
the sensor spec path resolves into an unmounted sibling repo, so NonLocalCorrelationSensor could not be constructed anywhere in this tree

salvage.keep: A cross-repo path should fail naming the MOUNT, not the path: ./fieldlink-sync.sh is the recovery and the FileNotFoundError never said so. Accepting an explicit spec= makes the class testable without the sibling repo, which is what let the other three findings be measured at all. The spec itself is deliberately not reproduced -- guessing its contents would put a fabricated standard where the real one goes.
salvage.killed: every use of the non-local sensor in this repository

screen.name: resolve-cross-repo-paths
screen.rule: A path into a fieldlink-mounted sibling repo is absent in a bare checkout. Fail naming the sync command, and take the data by argument so the module is testable unmounted.
screen.applies_when: a module reading a file from a sibling repository mount

claims.statement: scale is inferred from correlation_strength and technique is then selected from scale, so scale/technique agreement is 1.0 by construction: 0 mismatches over 21 strengths spanning [0,1]

salvage.keep: The remedy that worked for AISS's flat merit weights works here and did not require inventing a disagreement: report the degeneracy beside the answer, so a caller cannot read a tautology as a confirmation. Every metadata dict now carries scale_is_inferred. The general check is cheaper than the null: trace both sides of an agreement test to their inputs.
salvage.killed: scale/technique agreement as evidence of anything

screen.name: both-sides-from-one-source
screen.rule: When a check compares two quantities, trace both back to their inputs. If they descend from the same number the check cannot fail, and no amount of data will make it informative.
screen.applies_when: any agreement or consistency check between two derived quantities

claims.statement: the strength-to-scale map records a strong cross-system correlation as 'cellular', so the observation the sensor exists to catch cannot be recorded at all

salvage.keep: Scale is a property of the EXPERIMENT -- what was sampled, over what extent, across what interval -- and is knowable before the correlation is computed. Correlation strength is a property of the result. Deriving one from the other conflates two quantities with no stated mechanism between them. Passing scale explicitly was already supported and nothing called it that way, so the fix is a caller change, not a model change.
salvage.killed: the inferred scale as a description of extent

screen.name: can-the-target-observation-be-recorded
screen.rule: Construct the observation the instrument exists to detect and check the data model can hold it. An instrument whose encoding excludes its own target is not insensitive, it is blind.
screen.applies_when: an instrument with a fixed enumerated output vocabulary and a named target phenomenon

claims.statement: an inferred scale absent from the spec's scale_to_technique selected no technique and reported nothing

salvage.keep: dict.get(key, []) turns a vocabulary mismatch between two files into a silent empty result. Checking the four names _infer_scale can emit against the loaded spec at construction converts a silent miss into a refusal that names both sides.

claims.statement: the bifilar CMRR budget holds at an achievable matching tolerance
the 5 ps write pulse delivers 4.42 mrad at the legal on-chip coil field, 0.14% of a pi pulse

salvage.keep: The bifilar geometry and the common-mode budget are sound engineering and stand. What died is the direction of the worry: at 4.42 mrad the risk is not that the write destroys coherence, it is that the write does not happen.
salvage.killed: the concern that the 5 ps write pulse collapses spin coherence

screen.name: instrument-floor
screen.rule: Compute the signal in the instrument's own units and divide by its noise floor before designing anything around reading it.
screen.applies_when: any claim that a stated physical quantity will be READ by a named instrument

claims.statement: W is the identity, so the channels are independent scalars

salvage.keep: W = I is itself a usable fact: the channels are independent scalars, so anything built on cross-channel structure needs a different matrix, and SEED-5 shows one that is non-trivial while keeping proportions invariant.
salvage.killed: the claim that the seed influence matrix preserves structure

claims.statement: the claimed fidelity is 13 orders below the seed resolution

salvage.keep: The resolution comparison is the reusable part: state the seed's own resolution before claiming a fidelity against it. Thirteen orders is not a tuning problem.
salvage.killed: the stated seed reconstruction fidelity

screen.name: state-the-resolution-first
screen.rule: State the instrument's own resolution before quoting a fidelity against it.
screen.applies_when: a fidelity or accuracy quoted against an instrument or representation

claims.statement: the fix makes W non-trivial but keeps proportions invariant

salvage.keep: Carried forward as the working influence matrix. This is the constructive half of the SEED audit -- non-trivial W, proportions invariant.

claims.statement: the shipped strain invariants are blind to crystal orientation

salvage.keep: Invariants chosen for convenience discard the thing being measured. The recovery channels in the same spec are unaffected and were kept.
salvage.killed: the shipped strain invariants as an orientation-sensitive fault signal

claims.statement: the mechanical resonance correction uses thermal expansion where the modulus term dominates: ~20x too small and opposite in sign

salvage.keep: The general form is a comparison anyone can do before writing the correction: for steel alpha = 12e-6/C and dE/E ~ -2.4e-4/C, so a stiffness correction built from expansion alone is wrong by the ratio of the two coefficients. It survives a bench test because 0.024% against a +/-8% band is invisible -- which is why the check has to be done on the coefficients and not on the output.
salvage.killed: normalize_measurement for mechanical resonance

screen.name: compare-the-coefficients-first
screen.rule: Before writing a correction, list every coefficient that couples the quantity to temperature and compare their magnitudes. A correction built from the smaller one is wrong by their ratio and invisible in a narrow test.
screen.applies_when: any single-term temperature or environmental correction on a quantity with more than one coupling

claims.statement: two reference temperatures inside one module -- 20 C for the material and component corrections, 15 C for the acoustic ones -- and normalize_measurement crosses them

salvage.keep: This is the field guide's contraction table again, in executable form: percentages against an unstated baseline, back-solving to more than one. In code it is measurable -- normalize_measurement passes ref 15 C into r_correct, whose TCR is the copper value AT 20 C, biasing every electrical normalisation by TCR*5 = 2.0%. One module-level REF_TEMP_C removes it.
salvage.killed: normalize_measurement's electrical branch at its default reference

claims.statement: acoustic_f_correct uses the linear c(T) ratio and helmholtz_f_correct the exact sqrt(T_ref/T), for the same physics, with the docstrings swapped

salvage.keep: A Helmholtz resonance is an acoustic mode, so the two functions answer one question and disagree by 0.28% at -40 C. Keeping the exact form and deleting the linear one costs nothing, since sqrt is not the expensive part. The docstring inversion is the useful tell: the function calling itself 'simplified linear' is the exact one.

claims.statement: mu_water states no validity range, is 53% low at 100 C, and returns the 0 C value for every temperature below zero

salvage.keep: Two different problems in one function and both are worth naming. The exponential fit is anchored at 0 C and degrades monotonically -- +6% at 20 C, -11% at 50, -53% at 100 -- so it needs a stated range. And below 0 C water is ice: returning a liquid viscosity there is a category error, and a workshop at -40 C is exactly where a caller would hit it. A refusal is the honest return.
salvage.killed: mu_water above ~40 C and below 0 C

claims.statement: c_air(T) = 331.3 + 0.606*T is within 0.52% of the exact sqrt form over the -50..+50 C range it claims

salvage.keep: The correction the whole exercise needed, and it is sound: a prediction made at +20 C and read at -40 C is 10.6% off in frequency, against a +/-8% acoustic band. Worth carrying the error figure rather than the word 'valid', because 0.5% is fine against 8% and not against a 1% electrical band -- the same number is adequate and inadequate depending on the claim it feeds.

claims.statement: on the shipped fixture the two failing scopes report no time-to-failure and the only prediction belongs to the stable one

salvage.keep: The fastest possible audit of a reporting tool: run it on data built to exercise it and read the headline. Here every downstream defect surfaces in three lines -- the failing channels hit the None branch, and the noisy one gets 1950.8 days extrapolated from an R^2 of 0.294 quoted to a tenth of a day.
salvage.killed: the trend report's fail_in column as a planning input

claims.statement: fail_threshold = predicted*(1 + 2*tol_frac) is an upper edge only, so a downward drift is never classified failed

salvage.keep: A tolerance band has two edges and a drift detector needs both; the measured case is a value fallen 95% below its claim still reported 'drifting'. Whichever edge the drift approaches is the one to time against, which also fixes TRD-2 -- the two are one repair.
salvage.killed: the trend verdict for any downward-drifting scope

screen.name: enumerate-reachable-outputs
screen.rule: For a classifier with a fixed output set, list the outputs no input can produce before trusting the label set. A rule constraining both a term and the sum that term belongs to is the common case, and it is decidable by inspection.
screen.applies_when: a classifier or encoder whose outputs are a fixed enumerable set

claims.statement: when the value is already past the threshold and falling, predicted_fail_days is the time to come back INSIDE the band

salvage.keep: A field named for one quantity carrying another, and the sign convention is the whole bug: `current > fail_threshold` already means failed, so the branch cannot be about failing. Measured at 10.0 days on a value failing throughout. Same repair as TRD-1.

claims.statement: no minimum-sample gate: two points give R^2 = 1.0 by construction, so any pair of readings classifies as drifting or accelerating

salvage.keep: The FCL-3/4 shape in a new folder: a threshold on a fit statistic with no sample-count guard, on a series whose normal length is short. The arithmetic is the argument -- the residual sum of squares of a line through two points is exactly zero, so R^2 = 1.0 carries no information at n = 2 and the r2 > 0.5 and r2 > 0.7 branches are unguarded.
salvage.killed: the drifting and accelerating verdicts below ~5 points

screen.name: measure-the-null
screen.rule: Run the gate on data where the answer is known to be no, and count. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and a threshold with no measured false-alarm rate is not calibrated in either direction.
screen.applies_when: any threshold, gate or detector emitting a pass/fail or a score read as a rate, whose false-positive rate has not been counted on data where the answer is known to be no

claims.statement: the stable gate abs(slope) < 1e-6 compares per-day changes in ohms, hertz and kelvin against one absolute constant

salvage.keep: A relative slope -- slope divided by the claim's predicted value -- is dimensionless and comparable across every domain in the ledger. The same 1e-5/day is 0.036% per year of a 10-ohm claim and 365% per year of a 0.001-unit one, so the current gate calls the second stable.
salvage.killed: the stable verdict as comparable across domains

claims.statement: cross_domain_correlation gates on |r| > 0.6 with no null; any two monotone drifts correlate at ~1 whatever their cause

salvage.keep: Measured at exactly r = 1.0000 between two straight ramps with no stated physical link -- so the gate is reporting that both series are functions of time, which was already known. Detrending each series first, or shuffling one against the other to get a null, are the two standard repairs and the field loop needed both for FCL-5.
salvage.killed: the correlation gate as evidence of a cross-domain mechanism

screen.name: measure-the-null
screen.rule: Run the gate on data where the answer is known to be no, and count. 'Too permissive' in a comment is not a number, and a threshold with no measured false-alarm rate is not calibrated in either direction.
screen.applies_when: any threshold, gate or detector emitting a pass/fail or a score read as a rate, whose false-positive rate has not been counted on data where the answer is known to be no

claims.statement: the overlap is an exact float-timestamp set intersection and the defaults compare electrical against thermal, so the one correlated pair in the fixture is never tested

salvage.keep: Two independent reasons the function returns nothing on real data, and either alone would hide the other. Binning timestamps to a tolerance is the fix for the first; iterating over all domain pairs, with a multiplicity correction, is the fix for the second -- and the correction is needed anyway once TRD-5 has a null.
salvage.killed: an empty correlation list as evidence of no correlation

claims.statement: trend.py's LEDGER is a relative path, like the 24 sites in bridge.py and fabrication/

salvage.keep: Now 25 sites. The count is the argument for moving them together rather than one at a time: each new module that opens the ledger by relative path makes the split harder to close. Open problem GI-10.

claims.statement: Equilateral minimises worst-case strength of figure, at exactly 1.0
Surviving long-lived stone/timber nets skew near-equilateral by selection, not necessarily design
Closure failure and record drift are separable: closure tests the observation, drift tests the figure
Angle-only storage removes all metrological dependency; only SIZE needs a preserved datum
sp3 readout is rank-deficient

salvage.keep: Rank deficiency is checkable by construction, and TTM-3 supplies the fix: the six <110> directions are a complete basis. One audit produced both the refutation and its replacement.
salvage.killed: sp3 directions as a complete readout basis

claims.statement: the six <110> directions are a complete readout basis

salvage.keep: The constructive replacement for TTM-2, and it fixed three separate readout failures at once.

claims.statement: the vacuum criterion 'at least one mode survives' is true by construction

salvage.keep: VAC-2's mode-count floor is real and survives. What died is the criterion, not the folder: restating 'at least one mode survives' as a count with a floor makes it able to fail.
salvage.killed: 'at least one mode survives' as a vacuum criterion

screen.name: null-harness
screen.rule: Replace the structure you claim is doing the work with noise of the same shape. If the result survives, it was the shape.
screen.applies_when: any claim whose evidence is statistical, or whose structure could be replaced by noise of the same shape

causes.MATH_ERROR: the derivation is wrong. The algebra is reusable once corrected, and the error itself usually generalises into a screen.
causes.CODE_ERROR: the implementation contradicts its own specification. The spec is often still right.
causes.PHYSICS_BOUND: a real physical limit forbids it. The bound is a reusable screen for the whole class of proposal.
causes.SYMMETRY_FORBIDDEN: the material's symmetry forbids the mechanism. Free to check, and it generalises to every material of that point group.
causes.UNFALSIFIABLE: no input could have made it fail. What survives is whatever it was gesturing at, restated so it can fail.
causes.NULL_ARTIFACT: noise of the same shape reproduces it. The structure may still be useful for something other than what was claimed.
causes.UNITS: a dimensional error. The quantities are usually fine; the comparison was not.
causes.SUPERSEDED: replaced by something that does the job better. `keep` names what carried over.
causes.OUT_OF_SCOPE: not wrong, and not this project's question any more.

salvage_rule: A claim recorded dead MUST carry salvage.keep. A dead claim that records nothing recyclable is one somebody deleted rather than learned from. Refutations carry salvage too: `killed` names the proposal that died, and `keep` says what of it survives. Being wrong is expensive; the arithmetic, the bound, the sound half of the design and the error's own general form are the return on it.
screen_note: A screen is the reusable half of a refutation: the two-line check that kills the whole CLASS of claim, not just the one that died. Screens with reach >= 2 have already proved they generalise, and the ones not yet mechanised are the highest-value work in this file -- each is a mistake this archive has already paid for once.
applies_when_note: A screen is not universally applicable. `applies_when` states the precondition, and it is the field that keeps explore.py's coverage matrix from becoming a suggestion generator: the tool shows which screens have never been carried into which families, and a human reads the precondition to decide whether the empty cell is a real gap or a category error.
